theorems.name: Submission.f036cc6b1f_fd_coeff_decay
theorems.statement: ∀ (Γ : Subgroup (Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) ℝ)) (k : ℤ) (f : ModularForm Γ k), (1 : ℝ) ∈ Γ.strictPeriods → ∀ b : ℕ, (∀ n : ℕ, n ≤ b → (UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion 1 f).coeff n = 0) ↔ ∃ C Y : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ z : UpperHalfPlane, Y ≤ z.im → ‖f z‖ ≤ C * Real.exp (-2 * Real.pi * ((b + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) * z.im)
theorems.natural_summary: The analytic cusp function has vanishing coefficients through b exactly when its order is at least b+1. Factoring out q^(b+1) and bounding the remaining analytic factor gives uniform exponential decay. Conversely, the inverse q-parameter transfers decay to a punctured neighborhood of zero; a smaller finite order would force its nonzero leading factor to tend to zero, a contradiction.
